Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

Do not add a greeting, subject, signature, conclusion, or fact that the input did not supply.", "input": "i am writing to ask whether the Cedar Room branch can lend our neighborhood history group one flatbed scanner for the weekend of April 17 through April 20, 2026. We have a digitizing session planned for Saturday, April 18, in the branch's second-floor meeting room, and the scanner would be used for paper photographs and loose documents, not bound books. I am coordinating the session with two volunteers, Lena Ortiz and Mark Bell, and we expect six participants in total. We do not need staff to attend the session, but we would need the scanner's basic setup sheet and the correct power cable with it.

The group is working with materials from the former Harbor Street market, including family snapshots, price cards, and a small set of handwritten stall notes. The owner of the materials has agreed that we may make working scans for the group archive, but has not given permission for us to post images online. We will keep the originals in their existing folders while we scan them, and we will return every folder to the owner after the session. I have asked participants not to bring additional photographs from home, so the session stays within the materials we have permission to use.

For the scanning profile, please leave the existing setting unchanged if it already supports color scans at 300 dpi. If it does not, could the loan desk tell me what settings are available before the scanner is collected? I am not asking the library to create a new profile. The file name we use for our checklist is below, and I would like it kept exactly as written when it is entered in the loan note:
winter-kit-list.txt
I know that file is only our checklist name, not a scanner setting, but putting the two details together should help us keep the setup instructions and the packing list straight.

The meeting room booking is currently requested for 9:30 a.m. to 1:30 p.m. on Saturday, April 18; I have not received confirmation yet. If the room booking is not confirmed by Thursday, April 16, at noon, we will not collect the scanner on Friday, April 17. In that case, I will contact the loan desk to ask whether a later collection is possible, rather than assuming that the reservation can be moved. If we do receive confirmation by that time, Lena can collect the scanner after 3:00 p.m. on Friday. Mark is not available to collect equipment that day, so please do not list him as the pickup person.

For the loan record, these are the details I have so far:
1. One scanner is requested for the three-night period from Friday, April 17, through Monday, April 20; the number refers to the scanner, not to the people using it.
2. The scanner should include one power cable and one basic setup sheet. We can bring our own extension lead, so none is needed from the library.
3. The intended use is scanning loose paper items during the four-hour room booking on Saturday, April 18. We are not requesting a loan of a computer or any scanning software.
4. Lena Ortiz is the proposed collector if the room booking is confirmed by the stated deadline. I will be present during the session, and Mark Bell will help participants handle the folders.
5. We would return the scanner to the loan desk by 10:00 a.m. on Monday, April 20, unless the desk gives us a different return time. I have not checked whether the desk is open at that hour, so please tell me if that time is not possible.

We have a simple work order for the session, because the photographs and notes have different handling needs. First we will scan the price cards, since they are flat and can be placed one at a time on the glass. Then we will scan the loose photographs, keeping each small group in the order in which it was found. Last we will scan the handwritten stall notes, which have pencil marks near the edges. Mark suggested placing a clean sheet behind each note, and I agreed that we should do that only if the setup sheet says it is safe for the scanner. We will not tape, trim, or write on any original. If a page does not sit flat without pressure, we will leave it unscanned and note that for the owner instead of pressing down on it.

The expected amount of material is about 48 photographs, 12 price cards, and 9 handwritten notes. Those are estimates from the owner's inventory, not confirmed counts, and we may find fewer items in the folders. We expect to save one scan of each item, with no duplicate versions unless an image is unreadable and we need to check it again. I have not chosen a file format yet because I would like to follow the library's advice about the scanner output. The group archive has room for the files, but that does not mean the owner has authorized public sharing; the scans are for our internal reference only under the permission we have.

Lena asked whether the scanner would need to be returned in its carrying case, and I told her I did not know, so I have included the question here. If the equipment is normally loaned with a case, please include it in the collection details. If there is no case, we can bring a sturdy box for the return trip, but we would need to know the scanner's approximate dimensions before Friday. We can carry the equipment from the branch to the meeting room by hand, and we will not use a car or leave it unattended outside. I have not assumed that the library can provide packaging or transport.

Please let me know whether this loan period and the requested collection arrangement can be considered, and whether the scanner can be configured for the work described above. If a different return time is required, or if the setup sheet rules out placing a backing sheet behind the notes, I can adjust our session plan. The room booking remains unconfirmed, and we will wait for that confirmation before Lena collects anything.
